target_paper.title: Assessing DxGPT: Diagnosing Rare Diseases with Various Large Language Models
target_paper.original_source: Table 3 (RAMEDIS, 200 cases) reproduced from data/scores_RAMEDIS_gpt4turbo0409.csv with the src/dashboard_scores.py counting: P1 107, P2-P5 29, P0 62 of 198 -> 54.04 / 68.69

generation.parameters: temperature 0, max_tokens 800, one user message = PROMPT_TEMPLATE of src/batch_diagnosis_v2.py with the Python list repr of the case's HPO term names; no system message, no seed parameter
generation.battery: 200 RAMEDIS cases x 3 repeats (seed_idx 0-2, identical requests); 600 calls archived

judge.original: GPT-4-0613 via Azure deployment 'nav29' (src/diagnoses_analisis.py), temperature 0, max_tokens 800; dead
judge.parameters: temperature 0, max_tokens 800, one user message = PROMPT_TEMPLATE of src/diagnoses_analisis.py with the GT cell as stored (list repr) and the full diagnosis text
judge.label_parsing: lenient (first P0..P5 token, P2-P5 -> P5) on both the original and the substitute verdicts; the repo's exact counting (198 denominator for the original) is reported alongside

drift_separation: Generator drift and judge drift are separated by design: judge drift = track 1 (archived diagnoses, substitute judge) minus the original verdicts on the same diagnoses (Table 3 / lenient re-count); generator drift = track 2 (new gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 diagnoses, median over 3 repeats) minus track 1 under the same substitute judge. The judgment uses the judge-matched comparison; the comparison with the published 54.04 is secondary because the original judge cannot be re-run.

data.cases: HF chenxz/RareBench, config RAMEDIS, split test: first 200 records of data/RAMEDIS.jsonl (file order)
data.license: RareBench: Apache-2.0 (HF dataset card license tag and GitHub chenxz1111/RareBench LICENSE); dxgpt_testing repo: MIT (Foundation29hub 2023)
data.citation: Chen et al. 2024, RareBench: Can LLMs Serve as Rare Diseases Specialists? arXiv:2402.06341
data.item_text_note: Apache-2.0 permits redistribution with attribution; calls.jsonl therefore keeps the HPO term lists; per_case.csv and the case_sha256 in each request meta allow an id+hash archive if needed
data.ground_truth: archived GT strings (Orphanet preferred names resolved by the authors); no Orphanet API call

drift.definition: judge drift = track 1 minus the original verdicts on the SAME archived diagnoses (lenient parser both; also vs Table 3's 54.04); generator drift = track 2 (median over repeats) minus track 1 under the SAME substitute judge. The two are additive: track 2 - Table 3 = judge drift + generator drift.

results.judged_by: automatic rule per card 'judgment' / ANALYSIS_PLAN section 1 (see result.json judgment.rule); human double-coding pending

reproducibility_frictions_observed: judge model dead: GPT-4-0613 behind the Azure deployment 'nav29' (shut down 2024-09-13); substitute gpt-4o-2024-05-13 in a two-track design
ground-truth disease names come from a live Orphanet API call with a hard-coded key in the repo; the archived GT strings were reused instead
the HF loading script (RareBench.py) no longer runs under datasets 4.x; data/RAMEDIS.jsonl was read directly from data.zip in file order
HPO term names depend on the ontology bundled with the unpinned hpo3 package at run time; release v2024-03-06 assumed (hpo3 1.2.0 era)
2 of 200 archived judge outputs carry literal quotes and are dropped by the repo's counting (denominator 198); a lenient parser is used for the substitute judge
repo scripts call HF, Orphanet and LLM APIs at import time; prompt templates were extracted with ast and verified byte-for-byte instead of importing
Windows checkout (core.autocrlf) turns the LF CSV blobs into CRLF, including inside the diagnosis texts; normalised back to LF
